results.title: Modularity Measure and Community Detection Algorithms – Nodus Labs Support Center
results.content: # Modularity Measure and Community Detection Algorithms. In the context of network science community detection is an important aspect of analysis. Most of the approaches are iterative: they scan the network to see which nodes tend to be more densely connected together than the nodes from the rest of the network. These nodes are then organized into communities. For example, InfraNodus uses Louvain community detection algorithm (Blondel et al 2008). It detects the nodes (words) that co-occur more often together than others and puts them into the same community (designated with a distinct color each). The communities are then ranged by size. We then range those nodes either according to the degree or the number of connections that each node has (default measure — correlates with the node's frequency) or betweenness centrality. ### Modularity Measure. This community detection algorithm comes with the modularity measure, which measures how modular the graph is (the higher the number, the more modular it is). When this value is higher than 0.4, it indicates a highly pronounced community structure in the graph. When the value is lower than 0.4, the community structure may be present, but the clusters are quite well connected to one another. ## Related articles. * Cognitive Variability: InfraNodus Bias Detector. * Text Analysis Workflow: Get an Topical Overview and Find Content Gaps. ## Comments. results.title: Community Detection Method: Significance and symbolism
results.content: Community Detection Method: Significance and symbolism. Significance of Community Detection Method. Community Detection Method, as described in Environmental Sciences, is a technique used to identify clusters within a network. It is applied to discover patterns, such as disease comorbidities, using computational algorithms. These methods can be based on various network properties like node density, degree centrality, and K-Means clustering. The approach often involves modularity optimization to effectively group nodes into communities within a complex network. Synonyms: Clustering algorithm, Graph partitioning, Network analysis technique, Graph clustering, Network partitioning, Cluster analysis.
